chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Any NumPy array has a number of attributes that describes it,

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: in addition to the elements it contains.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: One of the most useful one is shape.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Essentially, a tuple containing the number of rows and

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: columns or height and width of the array.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: We have already seen how to specify this when creating arrays.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: The shape of the array A would be five rows and four columns.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: So this is your array.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Now let's see how to access the shape of the given array

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: by using the shape attribute.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: A.shape will give you the shape of the array.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Let's run it.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Array.shape will return you a tuple with the first value specifying the number of

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: rows and the second value specifying the number of columns.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Next we will learn how to individually access number of rows or number of columns.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: A.shape would return the number of rows and

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: A.shape would return the number of columns.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Let's check the output.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Here you see that the number of rows are correctly extracted as five and

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: number of columns as four.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: If you have more dimensions, you will have additional elements in the shape tuple.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: The number of dimensions in an array can be found by simply asking for

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: the length of this tuple.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: A.shape will return a tuple and the length of that tuple would inform us what is the dimension

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: of the array.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: It rightly tells us that the dimension of the defined array A is two.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Okay.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: How about total number of elements in an array?

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Yes, for a 2D array, it will be the product of number of rows and columns.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: But if you had more dimension, this calculation could be a little complicated.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Fortunately, we can retrieve the number of elements directly using size attributes.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: A.size will give us the number of elements present in the array A.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: We can expect the output to be the product of the rows and

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: the columns, which is 5 into 4, which is 20.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Let's check it.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: As we expected, the output is 20, which means there are 20 values in the array.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Attributes like size and shape are very useful when you have to iterate over

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: array elements to perform some computation.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: You can also access the data type of each element using the D type attribute of the array.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: Let's check the data type of the values present in array A.

chunks.title: Array attributes
chunks.text: In this case, our array elements are of the type float 64, that is 64 bit floating point numbers.
